```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE)
library(plotly)
cars <- mtcars
cars$model <- rownames(cars)
cars$cylinders <- factor(cars$cyl)
cars$weight_lb <- cars$wt * 1000
correlation <- cor(cars$weight_lb, cars$mpg)
```

## A small dataset with a clear pattern

<div class="big-number">32 cars. One question.</div>

How does a car's weight relate to how far it travels on a gallon of fuel?

We explore **32 models from 1973–74**, using R's built-in `mtcars` dataset.

Weight is measured in pounds. Fuel economy is measured in **miles per US gallon**.

<div class="note">This is a historical comparison, not a guide to today's cars.</div>

## Explore the relationship

Hover over a point to identify a car. Click a legend entry to hide or show a cylinder group. Drag to zoom and double-click to reset.

```{r interactive-chart, fig.width=10, fig.height=4.5}
p <- plot_ly(cars, x=~weight_lb, y=~mpg, color=~cylinders,
             colors=c("#59dec5", "#ffd166", "#ff8394"),
             type="scatter", mode="markers", height=360, width="100%",
             text=~paste0("<b>", model, "</b><br>Weight: ", weight_lb,
                          " lb<br>Fuel economy: ", mpg, " mpg<br>Cylinders: ", cyl),
             hoverinfo="text", marker=list(size=12, opacity=0.9,
               line=list(color="#ffffff", width=1)))
p <- layout(p, paper_bgcolor="#101e30", plot_bgcolor="#101e30",
            font=list(color="#edf3fa", family="Arial", size=16),
            xaxis=list(title="Weight (lb)", gridcolor="#304056", zeroline=FALSE),
            yaxis=list(title="Fuel economy (miles / US gallon)", gridcolor="#304056", zeroline=FALSE),
            legend=list(title=list(text="Cylinders"), orientation="h", x=0, y=1.14),
            margin=list(l=80, r=25, t=45, b=70))
config(p, displaylogo=FALSE, responsive=TRUE, scrollZoom=FALSE)
```

## Heavier cars tend to use more fuel

<div class="big-number">r = `r round(correlation, 2)`</div>

The Pearson correlation between weight and fuel economy is strongly negative in this sample.

The **Lotus Europa** weighs 1,513 lb and achieves 30.4 mpg. The **Lincoln Continental** weighs 5,424 lb and achieves 10.4 mpg.

Cylinder groups also cluster in the chart. Weight and engine characteristics vary together, so this plot alone cannot isolate the effect of weight.

## What this chart can tell us

**A descriptive finding:** heavier cars generally have lower fuel economy among these 32 models.

**A limitation:** this small historical dataset is observational. It does not establish causation or represent the modern vehicle market.

**Try it:** return to the chart and hide the eight-cylinder cars. Does the downward pattern remain visible?

## Built with R Markdown and Plotly

Created **October 26, 2026** by Anubhav Gupta.

This presentation was rendered from R Markdown. The interactive chart uses the **Plotly R package**.

Data: `datasets::mtcars`, extracted from the 1974 *Motor Trend* US magazine. See the [R dataset documentation](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/datasets/html/mtcars.html).

[View the R Markdown source](https://github.com/anubhavgpta/plotly-fuel-economy-2026/blob/main/index.Rmd)

<div class="note">Use the left and right arrow keys to move between slides. Creation date refers to this document, not the historical data.</div>


<script>
(function () {
  function fitChart() {
    document.querySelectorAll('.js-plotly-plot').forEach(function (el) {
      if (!el.dataset.eventsBound) { el.addEventListener("click", function(e) { e.stopPropagation(); }); el.addEventListener("dblclick", function(e) { e.stopPropagation(); }); el.dataset.eventsBound = "true"; }
      if (!el.getClientRects().length || !window.Plotly) return;
      var width = Math.max(260, Math.min(1100, window.innerWidth - (window.innerWidth < 700 ? 80 : 160)));
      if (el.dataset.fittedWidth !== String(width)) {
        el.dataset.fittedWidth = String(width);
        Plotly.relayout(el, {width: width, height: 360, autosize: false});
      }
    });
  }
  window.addEventListener('resize', fitChart);
  window.addEventListener('hashchange', fitChart);
  setInterval(fitChart, 500);
})();
</script>
